title: Towards Test Time Adaptation via Calibrated Entropy Minimization

problem.claim: Environmental changes and variability and noise in real-world data create a performance gap between training and testing phases.

gap.claim: Existing test-time adaptation methods use only the largest logit as a pseudo-label and minimize prediction entropy, which can make models overconfident in local test scenarios.

contributions.claim: The study introduces Calibrated Entropy Test-Time Adaptation, a confidence-calibration loss that considers both the largest and next-highest-ranked logits to balance overconfidence and underconfidence.
The proposed loss incorporates a sample-wise regularization term.
The study provides a theoretical foundation for the proposed loss function.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce a novel confidence-calibration loss function called Calibrated Entropy Test-Time Adaptation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their method outperformed existing strategies on benchmark corruption datasets across multiple models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Robust models need to generalize under environmental changes, but real-world variability and noise cause a training-testing performance gap.
Test-time-domain adaptation adapts source-pretrained models to target domains using unlabeled test data.
Existing methods use the largest logit as a pseudo-label and minimize entropy, increasing predictive confidence and risking local overconfidence.
CETA uses the largest and next-highest-ranked logits with sample-wise regularization to balance confidence, and includes a theoretical foundation.
The authors report improved performance over existing strategies on benchmark corruption datasets across multiple models.

source_observation.claim: Minimizing predictive entropy based only on the largest logit can produce overconfident predictions in local test scenarios.

interpretation.claim: Confidence optimization may require calibration constraints rather than maximizing confidence alone.

application.claim: When adapting models at test time, incorporate information from competing high-probability predictions and sample-wise regularization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported benchmark corruption datasets, models, or settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark corruption datasets or models.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical assumptions or guarantees.
